subtitle: How Devagiri’s hidden gold bought the throne of Delhi

panels.shot: split-panel wide, half showing Alauddin atop a northern rampart with Delhi behind him, half showing Ramachandra on Devagiri’s hill-fort above the Deccan plain
panels.action: Alauddin Khalji stands in armored poise on a cold Delhi battlement, eyes fixed southward, while far away Ramachandra Yadava gazes warily from the stone heights of Devagiri, the vast Deccan plateau stretching below.

dialogue.text: In 1296, a hidden road of gold runs from Devagiri’s hill-fort to Delhi’s throne—Alauddin Khalji and Ramachandra Yadava will both ride it, but only one will reach a crown.

i18n.hi: १२९६ में देवगिरि के किले से दिल्ली के तख़्त तक सोने की गुप्त राह चलती है — अलाउद्दीन ख़िलजी और रामचंद्र यादव दोनों उस पर सवार हैं, पर मुकुट एक को ही मिलेगा

panels.shot: medium close-up on Alauddin in a dim Delhi hall, half-lit, as an elder Jalaluddin sits in the background blurred
panels.action: In a shadowed hall of Delhi, Alauddin stands rigid in mail and turban, his face young yet hard, while behind him the older Sultan Jalaluddin sits on a simple throne, his outline faint in the dimness.

dialogue.text: Barani tells of a restless nephew in Delhi—Alauddin, governor of Kara—watching his uncle Sultan Jalaluddin grow cautious as the treasury thins and frontier foes press.

i18n.hi: बरनी लिखता है—दिल्ली में बेचैन भतीजा अलाउद्दीन, कारा का सूबेदार, देखता है कि उसका मामा सुल्तान जलालुद्दीन ख़ज़ाने के सूखते ही डरपोक होता जा रहा है, जबकि सरहदों पर दुश्मन चढ़ते हैं

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder shot from behind Alauddin, looking at a map spread on a low carpet, north and south marked with pebbles
panels.action: Alauddin kneels over a rough map on a carpeted floor, pebbles and small knives marking routes, as he traces a line southwards with a calloused finger, his brows furrowed in calculation.

dialogue.text: The chronicles say he dreams not of border raids but of a throne, and knows a fact every Delhi commander whispers—without new treasure, ambition is only dust.

i18n.hi: इतिहास कहता है, उसकी नज़र सरहद नहीं, सिंहासन पर है; और वह वह राज़ जानता है जिसे हर अमीर फुसफुसाता है—नया ख़ज़ाना न हो, तो हसरत सिर्फ़ धूल है

panels.shot: wide establishing shot of Devagiri hill-fort dominating the landscape, with Ramachandra in the foreground
panels.action: On a sun-baked Deccan plain, the massive hill-fort of Devagiri rises in tiers of stone, and Ramachandra Yadava, robed and crowned, stands on a lower terrace, watching caravans of grain and goods wind up the slope.

dialogue.text: Far to the south, Ramachandra of the Yadavas rules from Devagiri, a hill-fort rich with trade and tribute; the Deccan’s wealth gathers under his walls, though no Yadava chronicle survives to sing his side.

i18n.hi: बहुत दक्षिण में यादवों के रामचंद्र देवगिरि के पहाड़ी किले से राज करते हैं; व्यापार और नज़राने की दौलत यहीं जुटती है, पर कोई यादव इतिहास बचा नहीं जो उनकी कहानी गा सके

panels.shot: medium shot of Alauddin before Jalaluddin in a tented camp, banners fluttering, soldiers beyond
panels.action: In a wind-stirred field camp, Alauddin bows before Jalaluddin inside a great tent, soldiers and horse-lines stretching behind them, as the elder Sultan leans forward, listening with a wary, lined face.

dialogue.speaker: alauddin_khalji_and_ramachandra_yadava
dialogue.text: “Let me raid the south, uncle—beyond the Narmada lies easy plunder.”

i18n.hi: "दक्षिण लूटने दो, मामा — नरमदा के पार आसान माल पड़ा है"

panels.shot: close-up on Jalaluddin’s thoughtful face, Alauddin blurred behind, soldiers outside
panels.action: Jalaluddin’s lined face fills the frame, eyes narrowed in thought, while behind his shoulder Alauddin’s figure stands still, and beyond the tent flap the silhouettes of spearmen ripple in the light.

dialogue.text: Barani records that Jalaluddin, mild and trusting, grants his nephew men and leave to raid—never guessing that Kara’s governor weighs more than coin in his plans.

i18n.hi: बरनी लिखता है, नरम दिल, भरोसेमंद जलालुद्दीन भतीजे को सिपाही और इजाज़त दे देता है—ये सोचे बिना कि कारा का सूबेदार सिक्कों से बढ़कर कुछ तौल रहा है

panels.shot: long tracking wide shot of a column of horsemen crossing a river at dusk, silhouettes against the sky
panels.action: At a dusky river crossing, Alauddin leads a column of armoured horsemen through waist-deep water, the horses’ legs churning, banners furled to hide their colours, their reflections broken on the current.

dialogue.text: So begins the secret ride. Khusrau and Barani agree—Alauddin slips from the north with a small, chosen force, heading for Devagiri without openly naming his true target.

i18n.hi: यहीं से शुरू होती है गुप्त सवारी। ख़ुसरो और बरनी दोनों लिखते हैं—अलाउद्दीन चुने हुए थोड़े से सिपाहियों के साथ चुपके उत्तर से निकल पड़ता है, देवगिरि को निशाना बनाकर, पर नाम ज़ुबान पर नहीं लाता

panels.shot: overhead wide shot of the column moving through scrubland and rocky outcrops of the Deccan fringe
panels.action: Seen from above, Alauddin’s column snakes through scrub and rocky ridges, the land flattening towards the Deccan, men riding in tight silence, shields slung, the heat haze shimmering around them.

dialogue.text: Day after day they ride, avoiding great towns and main roads. Modern historians note the boldness of the march—deep into the Deccan with no supply line, gambling on surprise.

i18n.hi: दिन पर दिन वे घोड़े दौड़ाते हैं, बड़े शहर, बड़ी राहें छोड़कर। आज के इतिहासकार इस सफ़र की बेख़ौफ़ी पर हैरान हैं—रसद की डोरी बिना, एकदम दक्खिन तक, सिर्फ़ अचानक धावे पर दाँव

panels.shot: first glimpse wide shot of Devagiri from the raiders’ perspective, partly obscured by trees
panels.action: From behind a stand of trees, Alauddin and his captains look out at Devagiri for the first time, the hill-fort’s ramparts cut against the bright sky, smoke and dust drifting above its busy lower town.

dialogue.text: At last the hill of Devagiri rises before them. The chroniclers say the lower city below the fort swarms with traders and storehouses—rich, but poorly guarded against a northern storm.

i18n.hi: आख़िर देवगिरि की पहाड़ी सामने उग आती है। इतिहासकार कहते हैं, किले के नीचे का निचला शहर सौदागरों और गोदामों से भरा है—दौलतमंद, पर उत्तर से आने वाले तूफ़ान के लिए कमज़ोर

panels.shot: chaotic wide shot of Delhi horsemen pouring into the lower city streets, citizens fleeing
panels.action: In a sudden rush, Alauddin’s cavalry pours into the narrow streets of Devagiri’s lower city, horses rearing at corners, merchants and townsfolk scattering, guards scrambling to close gates further uphill.

dialogue.text: Barani speaks of a swift strike on the town below. Delhi horsemen crash into the lower city, seizing stores and wealth, before Ramachandra can fully draw his strength up into the fort.

i18n.hi: बरनी लिखता है, नीचले शहर पर अचानक धावा होता है। दिल्ली के घुड़सवार नीचे बसती में टूट पड़ते हैं, अन्न और दौलत लूटते हैं, इससे पहले कि रामचंद्र पूरी ताक़त किले पर खींच सके

panels.shot: medium shot of captives—Brahmins, merchants, townsfolk—herded together under guard
panels.action: In a courtyard crowded with sacks and chests, a group of captives—Brahmins in sacred threads, richly dressed merchants, and common townsfolk—stand under the watch of mailed Delhi soldiers, eyes wide with fear and anger.

dialogue.text: Barani’s pen does not look away. He notes prisoners taken—Brahmins and merchants among them—and some put to death during the siege, the cost of Alauddin’s hunger written in human lives.

i18n.hi: बरनी कलम नहीं फेरता। वह लिखता है—क़ैदी बनाए गए, ब्राह्मण और बनिए भी, और घेराबंदी के बीच कुछ को मार भी दिया गया; अलाउद्दीन की भूख इंसानी जानों से लिखी गई

panels.shot: dramatic low-angle shot of Ramachandra at the fort gate, rallying soldiers, arrows ready
panels.action: From a great stone gate high above, Ramachandra stands clad in armour, arm raised as Deccan archers line the battlements, their bowstrings taut, stones and logs prepared to hurl down the path.

dialogue.speaker: alauddin_khalji_and_ramachandra_yadava
dialogue.text: “Hold the heights! Let the hill be our shield!”

i18n.hi: "ऊँचाई पकड़ो! पहाड़ी ही हमारी ढाल है!"

panels.shot: wide siege shot of Delhi forces attempting to press up the slope under missiles
panels.action: Armoured Delhi troops strain up the steep, winding path to Devagiri’s gate, shields raised as arrows arc down and heavy stones crash near them, dust and shattered rock filling the air.

dialogue.text: The hill itself fights for Ramachandra. Devagiri’s steep ways and strong walls slow Alauddin, and the chronicles hint at hard presses and reverses before negotiation opens a different path.

i18n.hi: पहाड़ी खुद रामचंद्र के लिए लड़ती है। देवगिरि की खड़ी चढ़ाई और पक्की दीवारें अलाउद्दीन को रोकती हैं, और इतिहास इशारा करता है कि कई बार उसे ज़ोर के धक्के और पीछे हटना पड़ा, इससे पहले कि बात-चीत नया रास्ता खोले

panels.shot: tense medium shot inside a hall on the fort, Alauddin and Ramachandra seated opposite, guards behind
panels.action: Inside a stone-pillared hall atop the fort, Alauddin and Ramachandra sit facing each other on low cushions, mailed guards and Deccan retainers standing stiffly behind, the air thick with wary silence.

dialogue.text: Barani and later Isami agree—the siege ends not with a stormed gate, but with submission. Ramachandra yields treasure and acknowledges the Sultan of Delhi, and Alauddin gains what he truly came for.

i18n.hi: बरनी और बाद में इसामी लिखते हैं—घेराबंदी फाटक तोड़ने से नहीं, आत्मसमर्पण से ख़त्म होती है। रामचंद्र ख़ज़ाना छोड़ता है, दिल्ली के सुल्तान को मानता है, और अलाउद्दीन वही पाता है जिसके लिए आया था

panels.shot: medium close-up of Ramachandra’s face, conflicted, as chests are carried past behind him
panels.action: Ramachandra sits rigid, hands clenched, eyes following as porters carry heavy chests out past him, his jaw tight with the strain of a ruler forced to buy peace with his own stores.

dialogue.text: We do not have Ramachandra’s own words. No Yadava chronicle survives. But the scene is clear in Delhi’s record—a southern king paying heavily to spare his capital and kingdom.

i18n.hi: रामचंद्र के अपने शब्द हमारे पास नहीं। कोई यादव इतिहास नहीं बचा। पर दिल्ली के लेखों में तस्वीर साफ़ है—दक्षिण का राजा भारी क़ीमत दे कर अपने राजधानी और राज्य को बचाता है

panels.shot: wide shot of pack animals laden with chests and bundles leaving Devagiri, Alauddin overseeing
panels.action: On the slope below the fort, lines of pack animals bear laden chests and bundles away from Devagiri, Alauddin on horseback overseeing the column as Deccan onlookers watch in mute resentment from the hill.

dialogue.text: Khusrau praises the haul without numbers; Barani links it directly to what comes next. Alauddin does not linger to annex Devagiri. He rides north, his carts heavier than when he came.

i18n.hi: ख़ुसरो माल का बखान करता है, गिनती नहीं; बरनी इसे सीधे अगली कड़ी से जोड़ता है। अलाउद्दीन देवगिरि को अपने में नहीं मिलाता, ठहरता नहीं; वह उत्तर को लौटता है, गाड़ियाँ पहले से कहीं ज़्यादा बोझिल

panels.shot: dark, intimate shot of Alauddin at night, counting and inspecting jewels and coins by lamplight
panels.action: In a lamplit tent, Alauddin sits cross-legged before open chests of coins and jewels, lifting a necklace with rough fingers, a hard smile flickering as shadows from the flame dance on his face.

dialogue.text: Under canvas and in guarded rooms, the treasure is weighed and sorted. Modern historians see here the crucial hinge—Devagiri’s wealth turning from southern hoard to northern war-chest.

i18n.hi: कैंप के तंबुओं और पहरे वाली खोलियों में ख़ज़ाना तौला और बाँटा जाता है। आज के इतिहासकार यहीं मोड़ देखते हैं—देवगिरि की दौलत दक्षिण के भंडार से उत्तर की जंगी तिजोरी में बदलती है

panels.shot: wide shot of Alauddin meeting Jalaluddin on a riverbank near Kara, greeting warmly, soldiers in background
panels.action: On a calm riverbank near Kara, Alauddin steps forward with outstretched arms to embrace Jalaluddin, who has crossed with a small guard; behind them, Alauddin’s well-equipped troops stand in ordered ranks.

dialogue.text: When the Devagiri loot is safe, Barani says, Alauddin invites Jalaluddin to Kara with promises of loyalty. The newfound wealth pays wages, buys blades, and gives his camp the glitter of power.

i18n.hi: जब देवगिरि की लूट सुरक्षित हो जाती है, बरनी लिखता है, अलाउद्दीन जलालुद्दीन को कारा बुलाता है, वफ़ादारी के वादों के साथ। यही नई दौलत मज़दूरी देती है, तलवारें खरीदती है, और उसके डेरे को ताक़त की चमक देती है

panels.shot: low-angle shot of Alauddin later on the Delhi throne, regally seated, Ramachandra shown in inset background paying homage
panels.action: In the great hall of Delhi, Alauddin now sits robed and crowned upon the throne, courtiers ranked below, while in a faded inset behind him Ramachandra is shown standing in respectful posture, hands joined, before a northern envoy.

dialogue.text: Soon after, Jalaluddin is dead by his nephew’s hand and Alauddin is Sultan. From then, sources speak of Devagiri’s ruler sending tribute—Delhi’s shadow stretching further into the Deccan.

i18n.hi: कुछ ही दिनों में जलालुद्दीन अपने भतीजे के हाथ से मारा जाता है और अलाउद्दीन सुल्तान बन बैठता है। इसके बाद हवाले बताते हैं, देवगिरि का शासक नज़राना भेजता रहता है—दिल्ली की परछाईं दक्खिन तक लम्बी हो जाती है

panels.shot: wide reflective shot of Devagiri hill-fort at sunset, half in light, half in shadow
panels.action: Devagiri’s walls stand quiet at sunset, one side lit in gold, the other in shadow, as distant riders move along the plain below, the silence holding both memory and foreboding.

dialogue.text: Barani, Khusrau and later Jackson all trace the line—one daring raid, no conquest yet, but a river of wealth that topples a Sultan, feeds an empire, and binds the Deccan to Delhi’s story ever after.

i18n.hi: बरनी, ख़ुसरो और बाद के जैक्सन, सब इसी रेखा को खींचते हैं—एक साहसी धावा, बिना ज़मीन जोड़े, पर दौलत की धारा जो सुल्तान गिराती है, सल्तनत पालती है, और दक्खिन को सदा के लिए दिल्ली की कहानी से बाँध देती है

title_i18n.hi: देवगिरि का सोना, दिल्ली का सिंहासन

subtitle_i18n.en: How Devagiri’s hidden gold bought the throne of Delhi
subtitle_i18n.hi: देवगिरि के छिपे ख़ज़ाने से खरीदा गया दिल्ली का तख्त
